examples.en: The baby's cheeks are so round and cute.
I picked up some round pebbles by the river.
Mom shaped the rice balls into little rounds for me.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 얼굴이 동글동글하고 눈도 커요.
examples.en: That friend has a round face and big eyes.

examples.ko: 이 아이의 동글동글한 글씨가 참 예뻐요.
examples.en: This child's rounded handwriting is really pretty.
After using the soap for a long time, it has become rounded.

explain: '둥글둥글하다'보다 작고 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이에요. 아기 볼, 구슬, 작은 돌처럼 작은 것에 잘 어울려요. 활용은 '동글동글해요', '동글동글한'처럼 해요.
explain_en: It feels smaller, lighter and cuter than '둥글둥글하다'. It suits small things like a baby's cheeks, beads or little stones. It conjugates as '동글동글해요' and '동글동글한'.

examples.en: When I turned on the light, the room quickly became bright.
The eastern sky began to get lighter little by little.

examples.ko: 새 전구로 바꿨더니 거실이 훨씬 밝아져요.
examples.en: Since I changed the bulb, the living room is much brighter.

examples.ko: 날씨가 좋아지면서 마음도 밝아지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: As the weather gets better, my mood seems to brighten too.
I edited the photo and the face looks brighter and prettier.

examples.ko: 해가 뜨면 하늘이 점점 밝아질 거예요.
examples.en: When the sun rises, the sky will gradually get brighter.

explain: 빛뿐 아니라 표정, 분위기, 성격이 환해질 때도 써요. 반대말은 '어두워지다'예요. '밝다'는 상태이고 '밝아지다'는 변하는 과정이라서, 예전보다 나아졌다고 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used not only for light but also when an expression, mood or personality becomes cheerful. The opposite is '어두워지다'. '밝다' describes a state while '밝아지다' describes the change, so it fits when something has become better than before.

examples.en: When the wind blows, the waves get rougher and rougher.
When a stranger came, the puppy became fierce.

examples.ko: 배가 고프면 고양이가 사나워질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Cats sometimes get fierce when they are hungry.
The child burst into tears at the angry look on his face.
The weather turned rough, so the plane left late.

examples.ko: 화가 나면 말투가 사나워지는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people's way of speaking becomes harsh when they are angry.

explain: '사납다'는 ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '사나워요', '사나운 개'처럼 바뀌어요. 짐승, 날씨, 표정, 말투에 두루 쓰고, 반의어는 '순하다'예요. '거칠어지다'는 피부나 말처럼 부드럽지 않게 된다는 느낌이라 쓰임이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: '사납다' is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it changes to '사나워요' and '사나운 개'. It is used for animals, weather, facial expressions and tone of voice, and its opposite is '순하다' (gentle). '거칠어지다' means becoming rough or not smooth, like skin or speech, so the use is a little different.

examples.ko: 이 색은 너무 옅어서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: This color is so light that the letters are hard to see.

examples.ko: 물을 너무 많이 넣어서 물감 색이 옅어요.
examples.en: I added too much water, so the paint color is pale.
I bought a pale sky-blue T-shirt.
You look natural because you wore light makeup.
The fog has become much thinner than in the morning.

examples.ko: 향이 옅을 때는 한 번 더 뿌려요.
examples.en: When the scent is faint, I spray it once more.

explain: 색, 냄새, 안개처럼 진한 정도를 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '짙다'예요. 묽은 커피나 차는 '연하다'를 더 자주 써요. 말할 때는 받침 소리가 달라져서 [엳따]로 읽어요.
explain_en: It describes how faint a color, smell, or fog is. Its opposite is 짙다. For weak coffee or tea, 연하다 is more common. It is pronounced [엳따].

examples.en: The baby's skin is milky white, so it's really pretty.

examples.ko: 아침 안개 속에서 호수가 우윳빛으로 보였어요.
examples.en: In the morning fog the lake looked milky white.
I bought a milky white ceramic cup.
That actor is famous for milky white skin.
The winter morning sky is hazy, like milk.
This paint is a white close to milky white.

explain: 순백이 아니라 약간 부드럽고 탁한 흰색을 말할 때 써요. 피부를 칭찬할 때 '우윳빛 피부'라고 많이 해요. '분홍빛'처럼 '빛'이 붙는 색 표현 중 하나예요.
explain_en: It describes a soft, slightly opaque white rather than pure white. People often praise skin as '우윳빛 피부'. It is one of the '-빛' color words, like '분홍빛'.

examples.ko: 동생은 화가 나면 말끝이 짧아지고 목소리가 높아져요.
examples.en: When my younger sibling is angry, their sentences get clipped and their voice gets higher.
When winter comes, the days gradually get shorter.
I got a haircut and my hair got a lot shorter.
I washed the pants and it seems the length got shorter.

examples.ko: 방학이 짧아지면 여행 계획도 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: If the vacation gets shorter, we have to change our travel plans too.

examples.ko: 시간이 부족해서 회의가 짧아질 것 같아요.
examples.en: We're short on time, so the meeting will probably be shorter.

explain: 반대말은 '길어지다'예요. 길이뿐 아니라 시간, 말, 글이 줄어들 때도 써요. '줄어들다'는 양이나 수가 적어질 때 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: The opposite is '길어지다'. It is used for length, but also when time, speech or writing gets shorter. '줄어들다' fits better when an amount or number decreases.

examples.en: After playing in the winter sea, my lips turned blue.
In autumn the sky is clear, so it gets bluer.
I saw his face turn pale blue from shock.
I played in the pool until my lips turned blue.

examples.ko: 물감을 더 넣으면 색이 파래질 거예요.
examples.en: If you add more paint, the color will turn bluer.

examples.ko: 오래 밖에 있었더니 손가락이 파래지고 아팠어요.
examples.en: After being outside for a long time, my fingers turned blue and hurt.

explain: '파랗다'에 '-아지다'가 붙은 말이라 '파래져요'로 활용해요. 추위나 놀람 때문에 입술·얼굴이 파랗게 변할 때 자주 쓰고, 놀라서 얼굴색이 변하는 건 '파랗게 질리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is '파랗다' plus '-아지다', so it conjugates as '파래져요'. It is often used when lips or a face turn blue from cold or shock, and a face going pale from fright can also be described with '파랗게 질리다'.

examples.en: The spot where I bumped turned a deep bluish bruise.
I got a blue bruise on my knee.
The mold was bluish-green, so I threw the bread away.

examples.ko: 멍 색이 이제 덜 퍼레 보여요.
examples.en: The bruise looks less blue now.
The deep blue bruise turned yellow after a few days.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 입술이 퍼레요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, and my lips are blue.

explain: '파랗다'보다 짙고 탁한 파란색이에요. 그래서 멍이나 추위로 변한 입술처럼 좋지 않은 느낌에 자주 써요. '시퍼렇다'는 더 강한 말이고, 활용은 '퍼레요'처럼 ㅎ이 빠져요.
explain_en: It is a deeper, duller blue than '파랗다', so it is often used for unpleasant things like bruises or lips discolored by cold. '시퍼렇다' is the stronger form, and it conjugates by dropping ㅎ, as in '퍼레요'.

examples.en: I have a lot of work, so things have gotten much harder lately.
Exercising outside gets harder in winter.
As the exam gets closer, studying will get harder.
I didn't give up even as the situation got harder and harder.
Breathing got hard when I climbed the stairs, so I rested.
What if getting to work gets harder after we move?

explain: '힘들다'는 지금의 상태이고, '힘들어지다'는 그 상태로 변해 가는 것이에요. 몸이 지치는 것뿐 아니라 마음이나 상황이 부담스러워질 때도 써요. 반대로 쉬워지면 '편해지다'나 '쉬워지다'를 써요.
explain_en: '힘들다' is the current state; '힘들어지다' is turning into that state. It covers not only a tired body but also a mind or situation becoming a burden. When things ease up, use '편해지다' or '쉬워지다'.
